summary.headline: Pakka reports H1 FY27 revenue of ₹241 crore, 13.7% EBITDA margin, with PM4 start-up slipping to December and commercial production targeted for January.
summary.overview: Management said margins and revenue are rising, with consolidated Q2 EBITDA margin at 14.2% and H1 revenue of ₹241 crore, EBITDA margin 13.7% and profit margin about 7.3%. Wrap & Carry revenue rose to ₹205 crore from ₹60 crore with PBT margin of 9.6% versus 2.4%, and Food Services turned EBITDA positive for the first time with H1 revenue up 38%. Project Jagriti slipped: PM4 start-up moved from October to December, with commercial production aimed for January. Q2 included an exceptional gain from sale of older machinery, and the call covered financing terms with Neo, the Guatemala plant pause, and promoter warrant conversion.

segments.name: Wrap & Carry
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹205 crore with volumes of 10,700 tonnes and PBT margin 9.6%. Interleaving paper share about 50% of the glass interleaving market; exports held at about 30% share; dry pulp sales added.

segments.name: Food Services (Chuk)
segments.commentary: Strongest H1 in history, with record monthly sales in August across B2B, B2C and export. Added 350 tonnes/month capacity via outsourcing; 10 new products added; now EBITDA positive.

guidance_outlook: PM4 commercial production targeted from January 2027 after start-up in December; Q4 FY27 PM4 utilisation about 45-50%, rising to about 75% for FY28.
Internal refinancing target around December 2027; existing plant EBITDA run-rate of ₹100-110 crore cited as the refinancing enabler, with management also citing ₹130-150 crore for refinancing sizing.
Chuk capacity to reach 550 tonnes/month by end of calendar 2026; in-house/outsourced mix to reach 30:70 by year-end.
Bigger flexC Base launch planned for January; Food Services to reach profitability and grow top and bottom line.
Management noted ~₹ 50-60 crore quarterly EBITDA would be needed under Neo deal framing; PM4 contribution target about ₹150 crore EBITDA at 60-70% capacity.
No new international operations to be taken up for at least six months; focus remains on stabilising Project Jagriti.
capex_capacity: Project Jagriti: pulp mill upgrade complete; recovery boiler and 15 MW turbine started and under stabilisation; PM4 trials ongoing with start-up expected December.

Total project cost about ₹750 crore; UP government capital subsidy of 22% on eligible plant and machinery; 15-year depreciation, roughly ₹3 crore/month once capitalised, ₹30-32 crore additional depreciation in next financial year.
CWIP about ₹734 crore as of September balance sheet; product development portion ₹10-15 crore.
Maintenance capex about 2% of asset block, with lower spend in year one.
Delivery-container capex about ₹1 crore for first set of coating and gluing machines, 10-12 tonnes/month per set.
Coater for flexC not yet ordered; Guatemala plant paused, with about USD 3-3.5 million engineering design spend treated as intangible.
demand_pricing: Reliance solar-glass interleaving order of about 200 tonnes at roughly ₹80/kg (~₹1.6 crore), potentially rising to 500-800 tonnes.
Customers said they would pay ₹5-10/kg premium over domestic interleaving paper.
flexC Base structure sold at about ₹110/kg initially as a discounted price; management aims for ₹140-150/kg over 3-6 months.
About 500 tonnes/month of outsourced flexC Base already sold; roughly one-sixth of PM4 output already in market.
Dry pulp launched to reduce logistics; around 300 tonnes/month goes to Chuk outsourcing partners.
Chuk gross margin about 25% at market-equivalent basis.

qa_highlights.question: What are the downside consequences of commissioning delays, weak demand or lower NSRs; when is commencement and first principal repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Start-up moved from October to December for component testing; commercial production aimed for January. No term-loan principal repayment until after June 2028; Neo special-situations loan has no principal repayment for 24 months (from June 2026 drawdown to May 2028); interest differential of about ₹25 crore paid in eight instalments from October 2027 at about ₹3 crore/quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk Neo sells the pledged shares; what is the cover and price trigger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Ayodhya plant excluding PM4 was valued at ₹710 crore by an independent valuer; about ₹400-420 crore borrowed against up to ~₹500 crore peak lending. With PM4 (~₹750 crore capitalisation), plant value would be ₹1,100-1,200 crore. Sale only triggered by event of default.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Reliance opportunity size, premium and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: First order ~200 tonnes at about ₹80/kg; could rise to 500-800 tonnes. Quality edge claimed over imports and domestic players; customers reportedly willing to pay ₹5-10/kg more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pending write-off on Chuk machinery and why is Guatemala not written off?
qa_highlights.answer: Seven old machines, two discarded so far, five left; about ₹2 crore per machine minimum. Guatemala: about USD 3-3.5 million engineering design treated as intangible; project paused; merchant bankers see no impairment currently; exports of moulded products from India have started.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the stock fall so much and what is the market cap view; SBI and Carnelian?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-money valuation at ₹272 raise about ₹1,100 crore, post-money ₹1,400 crore with zero debt; incremental ₹500-600 crore debt and working capital up to ₹170-175 crore would imply about ₹500 crore EV. SBI MF talks active until March 2026, quiet since; Carnelian has not sold per company confirmation. Management pointed to ~₹150 crore EBITDA at 60-70% PM4 capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Preferential warrant conversion timing and investor meet plans?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30 lakh warrants converted on 17 October; balance of ~8.5% promoter increase split across two years due to 5% annual limit under SAST Regulation 3(2); next tranche around April-May. Investor meets planned: Ayodhya plant in February, video conference next quarter, Mumbai around June.

qa_highlights.question: flexC Base trials, realisation path to ₹130-150/kg and PM4 utilisation.
qa_highlights.answer: Pilot trials done with a research institute in Slovenia and an European pilot; structure, ratios and chemistry finalised. Price reaching ₹140-150/kg expected over 3-6 months once market accepts quality. PM4 utilisation Q4 FY27 about 45-50%, FY28 about 75%.

qa_highlights.question: Refinancing: EBITDA run-rate needed and maintenance capex.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹100-110 crore existing-plant EBITDA run-rate supports Neo debt; ₹130-150 crore annual EBITDA viewed as a good refinancing level, with ₹30-35 crore quarterly mentioned as bank comfort level. Maintenance capex around 2% of asset value.

risks_watch: PM4 start-up slipped from October to December; commercial production targeted January; ramp-up curve 30-40% then 50-60% before full capacity.
Refinancing target December 2027 depends on sustaining EBITDA run-rate; debt post-PM4 expected at about ₹500-600 crore plus working capital limit rising from ₹90 crore to ₹170-175 crore.
flexC Base pricing (₹110/kg now vs ₹140-150 target) unproven at live machine; coating plans deferred and coater not yet ordered.
Neo pledge: management expects no sale but pledged shares remain a sentiment overhang; EBITDA of ₹100-110 crore run-rate needed.
Pending write-offs: five old machines remaining (~₹2 crore minimum each) and Guatemala project status; impairment not currently warranted per merchant bankers.
Upcoming promoter warrant conversion balance in next financial year; Reliance order scale to 500-800 tonnes not confirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum in Wrap & Carry and Food Services, but cautious and somewhat defensive on Project Jagriti timing, valuation and stock price; several answers were deferred to later quarters or unquantified (e.g., Chuk write-off, international expansion).

Food Services has had the strongest H1 in the history of the business.
We are aiming for commercial production from January.
Right now our heads are down and focused on starting up the project, so please give us until about January for the investor meet.

growth.why: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue ₹241 crore with Wrap & Carry at ₹205 crore and Food Services H1 revenue up 38%; PM4 (Project Jagriti) start-up slipped to December with commercial production January 2027 and Q4 utilisation 45-50% rising to ~75% in FY28, backed by Reliance order (~200 tonnes) and ~500 tonnes/month of pre-sold flexC Base, though the brief gives no quarterly revenue or EBITDA growth figu

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated Q2 EBITDA margin 14.2% vs 13.7% H1, Food Services turned EBITDA positive, Wrap & Carry PBT margin 9.6% vs 2.4%, and flexC Base price targeted to rise from ~₹110/kg to ₹140-150/kg over 3-6 months, though PM4 ramp at 45-50% in Q4 dilutes.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: PM4 start-up moved to December with commercial production January 2027 (Q4 FY27), Chuk outsourced capacity building to 550 tonnes/month by calendar year-end 2026; PM4 utilisation guided at 45-50% in Q4 rising to ~75% in FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Wrap & Carry volumes rose to 10,700 tonnes from 7,600 tonnes, about 500 tonnes/month of flexC Base already sold outsourced, roughly one-sixth of PM4 output pre-sold, and Chuk capacity rising by 350 tonnes/month.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Total Jagriti project cost ~₹750 crore with CWIP ~₹734 crore, coater for flexC not yet ordered, and a ~₹1 crore container coating line planned, but no new major capex is guided and Guatemala is paused.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it is on track for a significant milestone this year and Wrap & Carry profitability is improving sharply, but PM4 delay and Q4 utilisation of only 45-50% limit near-term upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: PM4 start-up already slipped from October to December, the ramp curve is 30-40% then 50-60%, and flexC Base pricing (₹110/kg now vs ₹140-150 target) is unproven at a live machine.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bigger flexC Base launch planned for January 2027 alongside PM4 commercial production, and Chuk added 10 new products already.

rows.label: Internal refinancing around December 2027
rows.why: Refinancing depends on existing-plant EBITDA run-rate of ₹100-110 crore, with post-PM4 debt expected at ₹500-600 crore and PM4 target EBITDA ~₹150 crore at 60-70% capacity.

rows.label: Reliance solar-glass interleaving order
rows.why: First order ~200 tonnes at about ₹80/kg (~₹1.6 crore), potentially rising to 500-800 tonnes, with customers willing to pay ₹5-10/kg premium over domestic interleaving paper.

rows.label: Old Chuk machinery write-off
rows.why: Five old machines remain at about ₹2 crore minimum each (~₹10 crore) after two were discarded, a one-off non-cash charge that is pending.

tone.note: Management was confident on Wrap & Carry margins, Food Services turnaround and the Reliance order, but cautious and somewhat defensive on Project Jagriti timing, pledged-share overhang and valuation; analysts pressed on commissioning delays, Neo loan terms, refinancing and the stock fall.
